The test image shows a tomato leaf with extensive brown/gray-brown necrosis covering most of the leaf surface, with remaining green tissue at edges and yellow-green transition zones. The lesions are large, irregular, and appear somewhat papery/dry.

Key features:
- Large irregular brown necrotic areas
- Pale green/yellow border between dead and living tissue
- Dry, papery texture to necrotic zones
- No clear concentric rings (rules out Early Blight)
- No visible spore masses

Top candidates: Late Blight (large irregular brown lesions, gray-brown coloration) or Verticillium Wilt (browning with yellow borders).

Let me view one Late Blight reference image.

The reference Late Blight image is an excellent match to the test image:
- Both show large irregular brown necrotic areas covering much of the leaf
- Both have remaining green tissue at margins with yellow-green transition
- Same dry, papery texture on necrotic zones
- Matching brown-gray coloration pattern

This strongly confirms Late Blight. The test image matches the symptom description: "infected leaves develop green to brown patches of dead tissue surrounded by a pale green or gray border."
